authority: Independent assistant judgments, not native-language or medical certification. Numerical reviewer confidence is uncalibrated self-report, not a probability of correctness.

grading.scale: Ordinal 0–4, higher better; null for unavailable/rejected delivery; no averages.
grading.rawOnly: Rejected observations retain separate raw-only diagnostic scores, never counted as delivered.

blindness: Fresh packets omit candidate identity, price, timing, old grades and fixture answers; each lane read the complete exact packet before frozen rubric examples. The exposed canonical scenarios are recognizable, so this is not fully blinded or unseen validation.

reviewers.name: FreshEnglishBaselineReview
reviewers.coverage: Read all 1,472 lines of the exact new-a-content-review.json packet before consulting the r2 frozen baseline-a rubric, version 1.2-proposed. Independently assessed all 10 uniquely identified observations across all four ordinal dimensions, inspecting every input, raw English essential/vocabulary/dialogue entry, parser result and actual normalized value. Explicitly separated the four rejected/null deliveries from their raw-only content assessments. Compared retained essentials and alternative flags for the two changed normalized observations, including the pottery afternoon branch and allergy refusal loss; inspected unchanged deliveries for semantic defects despite parser success. Findings use packet-root JSON pointers and exact substrings of the inspected values. No forced finding was assigned to either tea observation. No provider calls, edits, builds, tests, lint or formatters were performed.
limits: Independent assistant content review only; not native-language, pronunciation or medical certification.

This assignment covers A English content and recorded normalized delivery only. Target-language text, diacritics, readings, romanization, translations, lexical spans and downstream rendering were not present for assessment; absence of those B-stage outputs was not scored as an A defect.
Technical rejection conclusions use the packet's recorded parser outcomes and actual null normalized values; the parser was not rerun and production UI behavior was not exercised.
Alternative analysis concerns the explicit local-alternative meaning recorded in the packet. No unobserved UI selection or rendering behavior is assumed.
Raw content quality is assessed separately from availability. All four dimensions are null for rejected delivered output, not zero and not copied from raw-only scores.

Scores are ordinal case judgments, not aggregate grades or evidence about prevalence, general reliability, timing, prices, comparative provider quality or p95 performance. Candidate identities and provider measurements were not used.

The allergy dialogue finding distinguishes a misleading staff suggestion from learner endorsement; no claim is made that the packet demonstrates ingestion, a clinical outcome or an actual guarantee of safety.

reviewers.name: FreshTranslationBaselineReview
reviewers.coverage: Read the entire exact 7,498-line packet before reading the frozen baseline-b rubric version 1.2-proposed. Independently assessed all 10 unique B observations: two each in Mandarin, Japanese, Czech, Ukrainian and Spanish. Compared every raw essential/dialogue/vocabulary item with frozen English and actual normalized groups: 50 essentials, 88 dialogue turns and 50 vocabulary cards. Inspected all 47 supplied lexical source snapshots, occurrence references and exact UTF-16 spans; checked lemma versus contextual inflection, partOfSpeech and senseKey meaning. The three absent optional sources are Mandarin 价格 twice and Spanish reservar in b-pottery-es-new-2; none was represented as a false supplied span. Inspected all Mandarin readings and all Japanese ruby plus 36 explicit Japanese card romanizations, including source-snapshot copies. Checked quantities, time/route, negation, politeness, noncommitment, shared-utensil allergy intent, raw/normalized alignment and literal encoded orthography. All ten are actually delivered parser-pass records, so delivered scores are populated and no rejected/raw-only scoring was needed. No provider calls, edits, builds, lint, tests, formatters, old reviews or prior findings were used.
limits: Independent assistant content assessment, not native-language certification, qualified human adjudication or medical advice. Allergy review checks fidelity of communication and refusal intent, not clinical sufficiency or real-world safety.

Packet inspection establishes actual normalized string and reading values, not a live rendered UI or audio pronunciation. Literal HTML entities were not silently decoded or credited as correctly rendered orthography.

Mandarin citation-tone versus surface-sandhi conventions, neutral-tone variation and regional lexical preferences were treated conservatively; dictionary-tone yī was not automatically classified as an error. No external pronunciation audio or native-speaker consultation was used.

Ukrainian masculine забув is usable for a masculine speaker, but learner gender is unspecified. This limitation is disclosed rather than assumed to be a material mistranslation for every learner; elliptical instrumental dialogue in the second Ukrainian case was judged conservatively.

Scores are ordinal case-level judgments, not averages or prevalence estimates. These ten fixed observations do not establish broad reliability, latency, p95, relative model performance or production acceptance.
No outputs were repaired. Parser passes and mechanically correct source spans were assessed separately from semantic fidelity, spelling and pronunciation quality.

records.rationale: Coverage: essentials cover beginner status, Saturday, hand-building a small bowl, the two-hour limit, price, materials/firing and collection. The dialogue supplies ten o'clock, thirty euros and collection the following week, but does not explicitly confirm duration or finish the booking; these are modest progression gaps rather than missing core essentials. Correctness/fit: preserves learner facts and avoids same-day collection. Vocabulary: ten relevant reusable pottery terms, including hand-building and firing. Flow: the consecutive staff suggestion of a wheel class is unnecessary but the learner clearly declines it; the exchange remains understandable. There are 11 dialogue entries and the recorded parser rejects the response; normalized is null, so none of these raw quality scores represents delivered content.

findings.quote: Yes, everything is included. You can collect it the following week.
findings.learnerImpact: The quoted final reply is the eleventh dialogue entry. The recorded parser allows 2–10 and rejects the whole response, leaving normalized null rather than delivering otherwise useful pottery content. This is a contract failure, not an English meaning error.

records.rationale: Coverage: essentials independently express black tea, no sugar, conditional lemon, drinking in, price and card payment. Correctness/fit: the staff confirms lemon, gives 45 crowns and accepts card payment; the conditional request already communicates the learner's decision to take lemon when available, so a second acceptance is unnecessary. Vocabulary: relevant reusable words and the useful compound black tea. Flow: short, polite, coherent roles and complete staff replies. Raw and normalized content are unchanged; the repeated no-sugar essential is harmless reinforcement, not a material gap.

Coverage: essentials explicitly state severe peanut allergy and small-amount danger, ask about ingredients, oil/sauce and shared oil/pans, request kitchen checking and provide refusal if safety cannot be confirmed. A shared-pan question supplies concrete shared-equipment communication even though the generic word utensils is only in vocabulary. Correctness/fit: the learner does not accept removing peanuts as safe, but the staff's peanut-oil/removal response is misleading and its final offer addresses absence of peanuts without confirming shared-equipment safety. Vocabulary: specific reusable allergy and cooking-equipment terms. Flow: the learner's safety boundary is clear; the scene stops at further checking rather than a resolved meal decision. This is not an affirmative safety assurance or a demonstrated decision to eat. Raw and normalized are identical.

findings.quote: It has peanut oil, but we can remove the peanuts.
findings.learnerImpact: The staff reply frames removing peanuts as a response to a peanut-oil disclosure without explaining how that addresses the oil or shared equipment. The next learner turn does state small-amount danger and conditional refusal, so this is not an endorsed safety assurance. Nevertheless, the practice dialogue ends with further peanut-free preparation checking rather than explicit equipment-safety confirmation or a final refusal.

records.rationale: Coverage: raw essentials cover the whole task, but normalization retains only the first eight and removes both the price question and the available-times question. The complete dialogue still contains times, a 35-euro price and booking, so information is not globally erased; the independently usable essentials no longer support the required time-and-price agreement. Correctness/fit: learner facts, two-hour classes, hand-building, inclusions and delayed collection are otherwise respected. Vocabulary: ten relevant reusable pottery terms, unchanged. Flow: raw staff lines present morning and afternoon cumulatively; marking the afternoon line alternative creates a branch that says 'also' without its morning antecedent and then receives 'The morning class works for me.' The raw main progression otherwise completes the booking coherently.

findings.quote: How much does the class cost?
findings.learnerImpact: This raw ninth essential is absent from the actual normalized eight-entry essentials. Price agreement before booking is an explicit task requirement. The dialogue still gives a price, but the delivered standalone essentials omit the learner's price question.

findings.quote: What times do you have available?
findings.learnerImpact: The tenth raw essential is also removed. Together with removal of the price question, this leaves the delivered essentials without the questions needed to establish the required time-and-price agreement, even though the dialogue retains a complete booking example.

findings.quote: We also have one from 2 to 4 in the afternoon.
findings.learnerImpact: The inspected line has alternative:true, unlike raw. As a substitute for the preceding morning-class reply, it supplies only an afternoon time and loses the antecedent for 'also'; the next learner line nevertheless selects the morning class and the closing books ten o'clock. The main sequence works, but the normalized alternative branch does not.

records.rationale: Coverage: essentials independently cover comfortable walking shoes, European size 39, trying both shoes and walking in them, a larger size if tight, yuan pricing and a noncommittal hold. Correctness/fit: no invented hold duration or purchase commitment. Vocabulary: relevant reusable footwear and shopping terms, including try on. Flow: staff responds coherently to sizing, price and holding the pair; the embedded alternative is semantically a plausible substitute staff reply. However, that alternative property is forbidden by the recorded parser, which rejects the response; normalized is null. Its good raw content is not delivered content.

findings.quote: Here's the next size up.
findings.learnerImpact: The semantically reasonable alternative is encoded in a forbidden raw property. The recorded parser rejects this response at lines[5].alternative and normalized is null, so none of the otherwise useful footwear content is delivered.

records.disposition: technically_rejected; raw English usable with minor essential-specificity gaps
records.rationale: Coverage: essentials communicate comfortable walking shoes, both-shoe fitting, tightness, a larger size, price and a hold without committing to purchase. They omit the European size-system qualifier and explicit yuan wording, although both are supplied in the dialogue; this limits independent precision without removing the core shopping exchange. Correctness/fit: the dialogue preserves European size 39 and gives size 40 as the next larger option, with no invented hold duration or purchase. Vocabulary: relevant, but try is less reusable for this task than try on. Flow: coherent roles and a complete hold reply; the exchange moves to price without an explicit evaluation of the larger pair, a minor omission. Twelve dialogue entries cause recorded parser rejection and normalized is null; all delivered scores are therefore null.

findings.quote: Sure, I can hold them for you.
findings.learnerImpact: The quoted final reply is the twelfth dialogue entry in a response limited by the recorded parser to 2–10. Rejection leaves normalized null; the raw shopping exchange must not receive delivered scores.

findings.quote: Do you have a size 39?
findings.learnerImpact: The standalone essential drops the supplied European size-system qualifier. The dialogue explicitly restores 'European size 39', so the topic retains the fact, but learners using only essentials cannot state the intended system as precisely.

records.rationale: Coverage: essentials independently describe the small blue bag, Lviv-to-Kyiv route, today's 14:30 arrival, passport, lost-property inquiry and where to leave a phone number. Correctness/fit: facts and lost-not-stolen intent are preserved, but the latter dialogue assigns the traveller's questions to staff and the office-location/phone-number answers to the traveller, teaching the wrong roles. Vocabulary: generally relevant reusable words, though lost property and phone number would be more directly useful as compounds than isolated lost/left/number/phone. Flow: the first five turns work, then the role inversion materially breaks the practical interaction. Parser success and unchanged normalization do not correct this semantic defect.

findings.quote: Where is lost property?
findings.learnerImpact: The station employee asks the traveller for lost property's location; the next 'you' turn supplies office directions. The inversion repeats when staff asks to leave a phone number and the traveller grants permission. Essentials remain correctly usable, but these dialogue roles teach the traveller to give staff information the traveller was meant to request. Raw contains the same assignments.

records.disposition: technically_rejected; raw dialogue needs role correction
records.rationale: Coverage: essentials independently provide the supplied bag, route, arrival, passport, lost-property and phone-number intentions. Correctness/fit: facts are preserved without theft, a train number or recovery guarantee, but staff incorrectly asks where lost property is. Vocabulary: useful reusable terms including lost property and phone number. Flow: the staff's misplaced location question is followed by the traveller's different question instead of an answer; the final staff reply does provide the phone-number destination and points to the office, but the preceding role/progression defect remains. The string alternative in the last line independently causes recorded parser rejection; normalized is null. Neither the useful essentials nor the raw semantic defect is a delivered output.

findings.quote: Where is lost property?
findings.learnerImpact: The required traveller location question is assigned to staff, and the following traveller turn asks where to leave a phone number rather than answering. Although the final staff line points to the office, the raw dialogue still needs its roles/progression corrected. This content defect is separate from the technical rejection.

findings.quote: You can leave it with me.
findings.learnerImpact: This string-valued alternative property is forbidden by the recorded parser. The entire response is rejected and normalized is null, irrespective of whether the alternative sentence would make sense as staff speech.

records.rationale: Coverage: essentials independently cover black tea without sugar, conditional lemon, drinking in, price and card payment. Correctness/fit: the dialogue confirms lemon, 45 crowns and card acceptance without changing tea or adding sugar; the conditional lemon request needs no redundant decision turn after availability is confirmed. Vocabulary: relevant and reusable overall, although isolated black is less helpful than black tea as a lexical unit. Flow: the concise staff reply 'Yes, you can.' fully answers the card question, and serving before payment is not intrinsically an error. Raw and normalized content are identical; repeated no-sugar essentials are not a material failure.

Coverage: raw essentials explicitly include severe allergy, small-amount danger, ingredients/oil/sauce, shared utensils and refusal when safety cannot be confirmed. Normalization removes the ninth essential, the only explicit refusal, and that intention appears nowhere in the dialogue. Delivered essentials therefore need supplementation for the stated safety-boundary goal. Correctness/fit: remaining statements preserve peanut allergy and do not assert that a dish is safe; 'do our best' is not confirmation. Vocabulary: relevant reusable allergy, kitchen and confirmation terms. Flow: raw consecutive manager replies contradict each other if sequential; normalization plausibly resolves them as local alternatives, and either branch can precede the allergy statement. However, both raw and delivered dialogue stop after generic accommodation without practicing ingredient/shared-utensil checks or a confirmed-safe/refusal outcome. This is incomplete progression, not a claim that the learner actually eats an unsafe dish.

findings.quote: If you can't confirm it's safe, I won't order it.
findings.learnerImpact: This ninth raw essential is absent from the inspected normalized eight-entry list, and no dialogue line supplies an equivalent refusal. Delivered content retains checking questions but loses the explicitly requested boundary for what to do when safety cannot be confirmed.

findings.quote: I understand. We'll do our best to accommodate you.
findings.learnerImpact: This is the last dialogue turn. The practice exchange never reaches ingredient or shared-utensil questions, a concrete safety response, or the learner's refusal decision. Useful checking essentials mitigate the omission, but the dialogue requires supplementation to model the requested task. The sentence is not itself a safety guarantee, and the same incompleteness exists in raw.

records.rationale: Coverage: black tea, no sugar, accepted lemon, dine-in intention, crowns and card payment are represented. Correctness/fit: Padesát means fifty, not the frozen forty-five; Budu to tady and Budete to tady omit the verb/complement needed for the intended drink-it-here statements. Flow: the eight turns reach service and payment, but the dine-in exchange needs grammatical correction. Vocabulary: all five dictionary forms, noun/adjective labels and senseKeys fit; the five snapshots match their referenced dialogue, with spans [17,20)=čaj, [25,30)=cukru, [15,21)=citron, [26,32)=kartou and [11,16)=černý. Inflected cukru/kartou correctly support cukr/karta. Diacritics are present; pronunciation scaffolding was not requested. Raw and normalized retain the same substantive errors.

findings.quote: Padesát korun.
findings.learnerImpact: Teaches fifty crowns against the exact frozen English Forty-five crowns, so the bilingual price pair is false. The same substitution exists at /cases/0/raw/lines/3.

findings.quote: Budu to tady.
findings.learnerImpact: The standalone essential intended as I will drink it here lacks a lexical verb/complement; the learner must correct an essential communicative statement. The same incomplete construction occurs in dialogue 4, and Budete to tady in dialogue 3 has the corresponding problem. Raw and normalized both retain it.

records.rationale: Coverage: European 39, both shoes, tightness, one size larger/40, 399 yuan, deliberation and an independently usable hold essential are present. All-day walking is absent already from frozen English, so that limitation is not a translation omission. Correctness/fit: normalized dialogue 6 loses the demonstrative because raw [zhè] has no corresponding 这, producing 双鞋多少钱？; the other principal meanings and noncommittal ending remain usable. Flow: staff responses progress coherently, though the price question needs correction. Vocabulary: 鞋/码/舒适/试穿/价格, POS labels and senseKeys are appropriate; four exact referenced spans select 鞋 [11,12), 码 [6,7), 舒适 [6,8), 试穿 [16,18). 价格 has no source and does not occur in the phrases; this is explicitly absent evidence, not a false source. Tone-marked readings were inspected throughout; orphan bracketed syllables in raw are removed during normalization, while ordinary character readings survive. Character-level citation tones and neutral-tone variation are not treated as categorical errors. No explicit Japanese-style romanization is required here.

findings.quote: [zhè]双[shuāng]鞋[xié]多[duō]少[shǎo]钱[qián]？
findings.learnerImpact: The reading zhè has no written 这 to annotate. Normalized /cases/1/normalized/groups/0/dialogue/6/card/text actually contains 双鞋多少钱？, losing the this-pair demonstrative and leaving an incomplete classifier construction. Other orphan syllables are removed without this same lexical loss, so this finding is specific to the missing character rather than parser acceptance generally.

findings.quote: Hello, I need comfortable shoes for walking.
findings.learnerImpact: The frozen conversation never expresses walking all day, although /cases/1/input/answers/Situation supplies that use requirement. Translation should not be blamed for faithfully preserving this source limitation; the learner may need an additional phrase to communicate the duration.

records.rationale: Coverage: one Saturday place, beginner status, two hours/10–12, 40 euros, hand-building without a wheel, included clay/firing and collection in two weeks rather than today are semantically represented. Correctness/fit: literal HTML entities remain in normalized target strings rather than actual Spanish accents, ñ and opening question marks; this requires correction for written study. Flow: the coherent inquiry, clarification and booking progression is preserved. Vocabulary: barro, bol, torno and reservar are appropriate lemmas/POS/senses; cocción is not the correctly written dictionary form. Four snapshots faithfully retain the encoded dialogue and reference the correct occurrences: [24,29)=barro, [35,49)=cocción, [57,60)=bol, [88,93)=torno. reservar has no source, which is not a fabricated source. Normalization trims the leading space in raw line 5 but does not decode the entities. No ruby or romanization was requested.

findings.quote: Me gustaría reservar una plaza para la clase de cerámica del sábado.
findings.learnerImpact: The inspected normalized string contains literal HTML entity sequences, not accented Spanish characters. This affects every essential and many dialogue lines, including ñ and opening question marks, requiring correction for written learning. The raw strings already contain the entities; the packet does not establish an additional UI decoding step.

findings.quote: cocción
findings.learnerImpact: The firing dictionary card contains an encoded entity instead of written cocción. Its source snapshot and [35,49) span accurately select the same encoded text, so lexical linkage is mechanically truthful but does not make the delivered dictionary spelling correct.

records.rationale: Coverage: small blue bag, Lviv→Kyiv, today 14:30, passport, lost-property location and leaving a phone number are all covered. Correctness/fit: Ukrainian Cyrillic and appropriate polite requests preserve lost/left rather than stolen, with no invented train number or recovery guarantee; забув is specifically masculine first-person past, so reuse is speaker-dependent where English does not specify gender. Flow: identification, description, referral and location/contact instructions form a complete usable exchange. Vocabulary: сумка/синій/поїзд/паспорт/номер телефону have appropriate dictionary forms, POS and senseKeys. All five snapshots and refs match essentials; exact spans are [22,27)=сумку, [17,21)=синю, [30,36)=поїзді, [14,21)=паспорт, [24,38)=номер телефону. The inflected forms are valid evidence, not lemma mismatches. Raw and normalized agree substantively. No Latin transliteration or pronunciation layer was requested; none is needed to satisfy this input.

Coverage: severe peanut allergy, even a small amount, ingredient checking, shared/contact utensils, inability to confirm and declining the dish/order are all present. Correctness/fit: negation and peanut identity remain intact; essential 3 describes utensils used for peanuts while dialogue 4 explicitly describes contact, preserving the practical shared-utensil concern. Wording such as アレルギーが重度です is formal/heavy but intelligible; no medical assurance or visible-peanut-removal workaround is introduced. Flow: kitchen inquiry leads to uncertainty, refusal and no order. Vocabulary: 落花生/アレルギー/原材料/調理器具/確認する, noun/verb labels and senseKeys are appropriate. Five exact snapshots/refs select [0,3)=落花生, [7,12)=アレルギー, [7,10)=原材料, [7,11)=調理器具, [11,13)=確認; 確認 validly supports the suru-verb lemma. All 18 card readings and explicit romanizations were compared, including rakkasei, jūdo, genzairyō, chōrikigu, kyōyō and konnyū; no specific pronunciation mismatch identified. Raw annotations become intact Japanese orthography in normalized delivery.

Coverage: requested tea/sugar/lemon choices, dine-in intent, crown price and card payment are represented. Correctness/fit: the frozen forty-five is mistranslated as Padesát (fifty), and Budu to tady/Budete to tady are incomplete constructions for drinking it here. Flow: acceptance of lemon and final unsweetened lemon tea are coherent, but the dine-in exchange needs correction. Vocabulary: all five dictionary forms, POS labels and senseKeys are appropriate; snapshots match dialogue and exact spans select čaj [17,20), cukru [25,30), citron [15,21), kartou [26,32), černý [11,16). Dáte si do něj citron? is consistent with the lemon offer. Czech diacritics are retained; pronunciation annotations were not requested. Normalization does not remedy the numerical or grammatical defects.

findings.quote: Padesát korun.
findings.learnerImpact: Padesát is fifty while the paired frozen English is Forty-five crowns. The normalized bilingual card teaches the wrong numerical correspondence, inherited from raw line 3.

findings.quote: Budu to tady.
findings.learnerImpact: This standalone dine-in essential omits the verb/complement required for the intended I will drink it here. Dialogue 4 repeats it and dialogue 3 uses the corresponding incomplete Budete to tady. The learner needs correction rather than simply a stylistic alternative.

records.rationale: Coverage: all bag description, passport, route, arrival-time and lost-property/contact goals are present, including unambiguous direction in essential 1. Correctness/fit: Ukrainian Cyrillic, 14:30 today, lost rather than stolen, and absence of guarantees are preserved. забув is masculine, an unmarked speaker-dependent limitation. Flow: Яким поїздом? / Поїздом Львів — Київ is awkward instrumental phrasing after leaving a bag, but the intended train is understandable and the referral exchange remains usable without rewriting the task. Vocabulary: all five lemmas, POS labels and senseKeys fit; referenced essentials snapshots and spans exactly select сумку [22,27), синю [17,21), поїзді [30,36), паспорт [14,21), номер телефону [24,38). Inflection legitimately supports dictionary forms. Raw and normalized agree. No pronunciation/transliteration requirement was imposed.

Coverage: beginner status, one Saturday place, 10–12/two hours, 40 euros, small hand-built bowl without a wheel, clay/firing included and two-week collection with same-day negation are complete. Correctness/fit: polite broadly understandable Spanish preserves quantities and intent, with actual accents/ñ and question marks rather than escaped text. Flow: the learner receives details, checks collection and then books; the final name question appropriately continues booking. Vocabulary: barro/cocción/bol/torno/reservar are correct relevant dictionary forms, with four nouns and one verb and suitable senseKeys. All five snapshots/refs match their phrases, and spans select barro [20,25), cocción [31,38), bol [50,53), torno [74,79), reservar [12,20). Impersonal ¿Cuándo se puede recoger...? is a fitting contextual rendering of the personal collection question. Raw and normalized preserve the same usable content. Ruby and romanization are not requested.

Coverage: severe peanut allergy, no small amount, ingredients/shared utensils and declining the order remain semantically present, especially in Latin pronunciation. Correctness/fit: assigning たべ to 食 while omitting written べ produces normalized 食る/食られません/食ません rather than standard Japanese orthography. Peanut vocabulary romanization rakkakasei also disagrees with correct ruby らっかせい and phrase-level rakkasei. Flow: the inquiry-to-refusal progression is coherent; the final learner thank-you is more casual than the requested polite style. Vocabulary: the five dictionary texts, POS and senseKeys are otherwise appropriate. All five snapshots/refs identify the intended lexical evidence: 落花生 [0,3), アレルギー [7,12), 原材料 [7,10), 調理器具 [7,11), 確認 [0,2); the last snapshot itself contains malformed 食ません. Every one of the 18 readings and explicit romanizations was compared; most phrase romanizations pronounce the intended Japanese correctly even where visible spelling is defective. No negation reversal, allergen substitution or safety guarantee is asserted. These are raw-origin annotation/romanization defects retained, not newly invented by normalization.

findings.quote: 少しでも食ることができません。
findings.learnerImpact: Raw /cases/8/raw/essentials/1 assigns たべ to 食 and leaves only る outside the reading, yielding visibly malformed 食る. Related omissions yield 食られません in dialogue 4 and 食ません in essential 4/dialogue 6. The Latin phrases generally pronounce the intended verb correctly, but visible Japanese teaches incorrect spelling in the small-amount and refusal statements; this is not a demonstrated reversal of allergy intent.

findings.quote: rakkakasei
findings.learnerImpact: The peanut vocabulary romanization adds an extra ka relative to 落花生[らっかせい] and the phrase-level rakkasei. A learner with no Japanese receives conflicting pronunciation for the central allergen word. The erroneous value is already present at /cases/8/raw/vocabRomanizations/0.

findings.quote: 確認してくれてありがとう。
findings.learnerImpact: This thank-you is casual relative to the requested short polite restaurant Japanese and the surrounding polite sentences. The refusal remains understandable; this is a register limitation, not a safety assurance or a failure to decline.

records.rationale: Coverage: European 39, trying both shoes, larger/40 when tight, 399 yuan, thinking before deciding and a hold essential are supplied. All-day walking is absent already from the frozen English. Correctness/fit: simplified Mandarin is intelligible and noncommittal; 欧码三十九码 is redundant but understandable. 留一下 is a polite brief/softened hold request, not an invented specific duration. Flow: complete responsive fitting and price exchange ends without purchase. Vocabulary: 鞋/码/舒适/试/价格 and POS labels are appropriate; 试 is a broader reusable verb than English try on, with the shoe context supporting that sense rather than a universally exact standalone equivalence. Four matching snapshots/refs select 鞋 [11,12), 码 [6,7), 舒适 [6,8), 试 [14,15), the first of the reduplicated 试试. 价格 is correctly formed but unsourced and absent from the phrases. All tone-marked readings were inspected: yī before 号/下 is citation-tone notation rather than surface sandhi, and repeated syllables sometimes retain full tones; these do not justify a categorical defect without a specified transcription convention. Orphan raw bracketed repetitions disappear in normalization without losing written characters. No Japanese-style explicit romanization is required.

findings.quote: Hello, I need comfortable shoes for walking.
findings.learnerImpact: The English phrase set omits the supplied all-day walking requirement; the target faithfully preserves a less specific shopping need. This is a source-origin limitation rather than an omission introduced by translation.

disposition: Collection and independent assistant assessment complete. Preserve known failures. Human review decides suitability for an intended like-for-like comparison; no broader confidence, automatic extension, final baseline acceptance, model/prompt change, C or deployment authorized.
